# ISF Program Context: Climate Change Across School Years

> **Stage summary.** This section describes how student climate perceptions changed across the three data collection years: 2022--23 (pre-program baseline), 2023--24, and 2024--25 (ISF implementation years). All comparisons are purely descriptive -- factor scores are compared across years and schools to characterize the program context, not to estimate causal program effects. A vertical reference line marks the transition from the pre-program to the implementation period.

```{r isf-setup}
# ============================================================
# Label years as pre-program vs. implementation
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2022-2023: pre-ISF baseline year
# 2023-2024: first year of ISF implementation
# 2024-2025: second year of ISF implementation
# ============================================================

isf_year_labels <- c(
  "2022-2023" = "2022-23 (Pre-ISF)",
  "2023-2024" = "2023-24 (Year 1)",
  "2024-2025" = "2024-25 (Year 2)"
)

cfa_data_scored <- cfa_data_scored %>%
  mutate(
    year_label = recode(school_year, !!!isf_year_labels),
    year_label = factor(year_label, levels = isf_year_labels)
  )
```

## Overall Climate Trends Across School Years

```{r isf-overall-year-trend}
# ============================================================
# District-wide mean factor scores across school years
# Styled to match the staff plot
# ============================================================

year_means <- cfa_data_scored %>%
  dplyr::select(year_label, dplyr::all_of(factor_names)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    dplyr::all_of(factor_names),
    names_to = "factor",
    values_to = "score"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(factor, year_label) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n    = sum(!is.na(score)),
    mean = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    se   = sd(score, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(score))),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    year_label = factor(
      year_label,
      levels = c("2022-23 (Pre-ISF)", "2023-24 (Year 1)", "2024-25 (Year 2)")
    ),
    factor = factor(factor, levels = factor_names)
  )

ggplot(year_means, aes(x = year_label, y = mean, group = 1)) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dotted",
    color = "gray60",
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = 3.5,
    color = "#4e79a7"
  ) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.8,
    color = "#4e79a7"
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se),
    width = 0.15,
    linewidth = 0.5,
    alpha = 0.6,
    color = "#4e79a7"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Student Climate Factor Scores by School Year",
    subtitle = "District-wide means with ±1 SE bars",
    y = "Mean factor score (standardized)",
    x = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "plain"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11)
  )
```

**Interpretation.** This plot shows district-wide mean factor scores across the three school years, with a dashed line marking the transition from the pre-ISF baseline (2022--23) to the implementation period (2023--24 onward). Error bars show $\pm$1 standard error around each mean. Consistent upward trends across multiple climate dimensions from 2022--23 to 2023--24 or 2024--25 would indicate improving climate conditions coinciding with ISF implementation, though other factors could also explain the pattern. Downward trends or flat trajectories on specific dimensions point to areas where program impact may not yet be detectable, or where conditions deteriorated despite implementation. A mean shift of approximately 0.20 standardized units or more is generally considered substantively meaningful.

```{r isf-year-table}
# Numeric summary of year-over-year changes
# Use the factor levels directly (they match the column names after pivot_wider)
pre_label  <- levels(year_means$year_label)[1]  # "2022-23 (Pre-ISF)"
yr1_label  <- levels(year_means$year_label)[2]  # "2023-24 (Year 1)"
yr2_label  <- levels(year_means$year_label)[3]  # "2024-25 (Year 2)"

year_change_table <- year_means %>%
  select(factor, year_label, mean) %>%
  mutate(mean = round(mean, 3)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year_label, values_from = mean) %>%
  mutate(
    `Change: Pre to Yr1` = round(.data[[yr1_label]] - .data[[pre_label]], 3),
    `Change: Pre to Yr2` = round(.data[[yr2_label]] - .data[[pre_label]], 3)
  ) %>%
  arrange(factor)

print(year_change_table)
```

**Interpretation.** Positive change values indicate that mean factor scores improved relative to the pre-ISF baseline; negative values indicate decline. A change of $\pm$0.20 standardized units is a commonly used threshold for substantive meaningfulness. These are unadjusted descriptive differences and should not be interpreted as causal evidence of program impact.

## Climate Trends by School and Year

```{r isf-school-year-facet}
school_year_means <- cfa_data_scored %>%
  select(school_name, year_label, all_of(factor_names)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(school_name)) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(factor_names), names_to = "factor", values_to = "score") %>%
  group_by(school_name, factor, year_label) %>%
  summarise(
    n    = sum(!is.na(score)),
    mean = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(school_year_means, aes(x = year_label, y = mean,
                               color = school_name, group = school_name)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1.5, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted",
             color = "gray60", linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(
    title    = "Student Climate Factor Scores by School and Year",
    subtitle = "Each line = one school; dashed line marks ISF onset; dotted = standardized zero",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Mean factor score",
    color    = "School"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1, size = 7),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```

**Interpretation.** Each line represents one school's trajectory across the three years. Lines rising from left to right indicate improving perceptions; flat or declining lines indicate no improvement or worsening. Schools that improve consistently across multiple climate dimensions are the strongest candidates for attributing positive change to ISF implementation.

```{r isf-school-year-table}
print(school_year_means %>%
  mutate(mean = round(mean, 3)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year_label, values_from = c(mean, n)) %>%
  arrange(school_name, factor))
```

# Results Summary

```{r results-summary}
cat(glue(
  "STUDENT SURVEY -- RESULTS SUMMARY (v3)\n\n",

  "The MMSD student climate survey contains 43 items administered in both Fall and ",
  "Spring waves across three school years (2022-23 through 2024-25). After applying ",
  "a 70% item completeness threshold, the pooled dataset contains ",
  "{nrow(mmsd_students_common_fa)} rows from ",
  "{n_distinct(mmsd_students_common_fa$student_id)} unique students. ",
  "Students were randomly split into independent EFA and CFA subsamples at the ",
  "student level to prevent data leakage across waves.\n\n",

  "Factorability: KMO = 0.93 (marvelous), Bartlett chi-sq(903) = 23476, p < .001. ",
  "All 43 items passed per-item MSA screening (lowest = q380 at 0.702). The data ",
  "are strongly suited for factor analysis.\n\n",

  "Missing data: item-level missingness ranged from 0.8% to 55.5% across the 43 ",
  "both-wave items. The high end reflects q390 (after-school safety), which is set ",
  "to NA for non-participants. Median item missingness was 2.5%. FIML (MLR estimator) ",
  "was used for all CFA models; pairwise polychoric correlations with median imputation ",
  "were used for EFA.\n\n",

  "Reliability: five of seven theoretically defined subscales showed strong internal ",
  "consistency (alpha >= .80). School Engagement was acceptable (alpha >= .70). ",
  "The two-item Student Experience scale (alpha = .540) was excluded from CFA.\n\n",

  "EFA: MAP suggested 7 factors, parallel analysis suggested 8. VSS complexity-1/2 ",
  "peaks at 1-2 reflect a general school climate factor, not actionable recommendations. ",
  "The F8 solution was used for item screening. Four substantive EFA factors emerged ",
  "(Adult Support, Peer Climate, Fairness, Belonging/Engagement merged) plus four ",
  "response-format artifact factors within Safety and after-school contexts. ",
  "The automated EFA screen flagged: q391 (dropped -- no loading >= .30), ",
  "q392 (dropped -- even cross-load), q292 (dropped -- excluded Student Experience scale), ",
  "q257 and q384 (retained in CFA on substantive grounds).\n\n",

  "CFA: the final five-factor model (TeacherAdult, PeerClimate, Fairness, Belonging, Safety) ",
  "was refined across three versions. V1: full theory-guided model. ",
  "V2: removed q380/q381 (belong_4 format artifacts, weak loadings). ",
  "V3 (final): additionally removed q389/q390 from Safety (format-artifact EFA loadings, ",
  "weak v2 CFA loadings of .314/.397, large residual MIs). The v3 Safety factor ",
  "is anchored by q257-q261 (core school-environment safety items). ",
  "V3 fit: CFI = ", round(fitMeasures(cfa_fit_v3, "cfi"), 3), ", ",
  "TLI = ", round(fitMeasures(cfa_fit_v3, "tli"), 3), ", ",
  "RMSEA = ", round(fitMeasures(cfa_fit_v3, "rmsea"), 3), ", ",
  "SRMR = ", round(fitMeasures(cfa_fit_v3, "srmr"), 3), ". ",
  "RMSEA and SRMR meet conventional thresholds; CFI/TLI approach but do not reach .95, ",
  "which is typical for broad school climate surveys with a strong general factor. ",
  "All 31 retained indicators load >= .40 except q393 (PeerClimate, loading = .386), ",
  "which is retained as the only reverse-valenced peer climate item. ",
  "Latent factor correlations range from .560 (Fairness-TeacherAdult) to .851 ",
  "(Safety-Belonging), supporting five related but distinct climate dimensions.\n\n",

  "Factor scores: extracted from v3 final model. Factor scores are standardized ",
  "(mean ~0, SD ~1) and are available alongside row-mean scale scores (1-4 metric) ",
  "for all five dimensions. The ISF program context section describes pre-to-post ",
  "changes across the 2022-23 baseline and 2023-24 / 2024-25 implementation years."
))
```
